title: Better Die
statementMd:
You have a fair six-sided die with positive integer face values a1,a2,…,a6. Construct another fair six-sided die with positive integer face values b1,b2,…,b6 whose sum is exactly k. Face values may repeat on either die.

Roll each die once, independently. The new die wins if and only if its value is strictly greater than the original die's value; a tie is not a win. Determine whether you can make it win at least 19 of the 36 equally likely pairs of faces (that is, with probability strictly greater than 50%). If so, construct such a die.

## Input

The first line contains six integers a1,a2,…,a6 (1≤ai≤109), the labels of the original die.

The second line contains an integer k (1≤k≤1018), the required sum of the new die's labels.

## Output

If no valid new die exists, print `NO`.

Otherwise, print `YES` on the first line and six positive integers b1,b2,…,b6 on the second line. Their sum must be exactly k, and the new die must win at least 19 of the 36 pairs of faces.

The labels may appear in any order. If multiple answers exist, print any one. The strings `YES` and `NO` are case-sensitive.

## Note

For the first example, another valid choice of labels is 5,4,4,4,4,4. These labels sum to 5+4+4+4+4+4=25. Its face labeled 5 beats four faces of the original die, and each face labeled 4 beats three. Thus, it wins 4+5⋅3=19 pairs.

In the second example, a face must be labeled at least 2 to win. Each such face wins six pairs, so at least four are needed to win 19 pairs. Even if the other two faces are labeled 1, the sum is at least 2+2+2+2+1+1=10>9.
